semis.why: SOXX +1.07% pre (thin, pre-market has no volume), 18/0 names up, on Anthropic's IPO filing ($518B compute/infrastructure obligations). The gap already banks the positive half of a double-edged filing (same document: existential-risk warning, $42B 2025 net loss; futures wavering on it). Nothing added beyond the gap in the US chip names - the intraday extension is in European power semis, a different sub-group. 10Y at a 19-year high (5.24%) with an October hike priced caps multiples; JOLTS 22:00 SGT; MU prints Wed after the close. Stretch +6.9% vs 50d median. Mild.

big_tech.why: QQQ +0.38% pre after Nasdaq -0.9% Mon on yields; META +1.2% the only real mover. The most rate-sensitive group; with the 10Y flat at 5.24% and JOLTS the only print, no reason for a trend day either way. Mild.

market.why: SPY +0.22% pre, S&P futures +0.14%. Monday's -0.8% was the 10Y; today the 10Y is flat, oil -1.3%, VIX 15.9 in contango. JOLTS (22:00 SGT) is the only print before PCE Wed; direction hinges on the 10Y after it - a coin flip, logged as one.

sg_banks.why: STI -0.40% today but the three banks flat (+0.03% median) on 1.31x volume - they held while the index slipped. Tomorrow's close follows US tonight, which this read calls flat; no bank-specific catalyst (earnings ~36 days out).

summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have and don't chase the chip bounce. Tonight is a bond-market day: where the 10-year yield sits after the 22:00 SGT jobs-openings data decides it, and I can't call that.
summary.where_we_are: 20:00 SGT / 08:00 ET Tuesday. US pre-market, opens 21:30 SGT; Singapore closed. Next: JOLTS job openings 22:00 SGT, PCE inflation Wed 20:30 SGT, Micron results Thu 04:05 SGT, payrolls Fri 20:30 SGT.
summary.macro_attribution: The 10-year yield is the mover that matters: it hit a 19-year high near 5.24% on Monday and is flat this morning. Every lean below depends on it holding there. Oil is down about 2% to $91 and would help, but the call doesn't rely on it.
what_happened: Monday: S&P 500 -0.8%, Nasdaq -0.9% as the 10-year yield hit its highest since 2007 (CNBC, Sep 29). Rate futures price an October Fed hike (CNBC, Sep 29). That is the pressure on everything.

Anthropic's IPO filing shows $518B of computing and infrastructure commitments. European chip stocks rose on it (Yahoo Finance, Sep 29). The same filing warns of 'existential risks' and a $42B 2025 loss, and US futures are wavering on that (Yahoo Finance, Sep 29). It cuts both ways.
Chips are +1.1% pre-market, with all 18 names up (tape). Pre-market trades carry no volume, so this is thin until the open confirms it.

Power chips lead: Navitas +9% after a reported US Army silicon-carbide contract (Investing.com, Sep 28; article not opened); in Europe Infineon +4.7%, Aixtron +5.7% and Soitec +7.2%, still climbing late in their session (tape).
Asia was weak: Nikkei -1.2%, Taiwan -0.7%, SK Hynix flat (tape).

per_group.semis: Chips: flat from here. The pre-market gain already prices the good half of the Anthropic news, and the part still moving is European power chips, not the US chipmakers. With the 10-year at a 19-year high I see no reason for the gain to build or to fade.
per_group.big_tech: Big tech: flat. This is the group most sensitive to rates, Meta (+1.2%) is the only real mover, and a flat yield gives it no trend.
per_group.sg_banks: Singapore banks: flat. They held steady while the index fell 0.4% on heavier volume, and tomorrow they will follow a US session I expect to be flat.
per_group.market: Whole market: flat. Monday's fall came from yields; today yields are still and oil is easing. It turns on the 10-year after JOLTS.

change_my_mind: The 10-year closes above ~5.26%: Monday repeats, and chips, big tech and the market all go to slightly down.
The 10-year drops below ~5.20% after JOLTS: relief, all three go to slightly up.
Chips hold their gain through the first hour on real volume: chips go to slightly up.
Micron and SanDisk run well ahead of Wednesday's print: memory is being bought, which lifts chips.
summary.confidence: low, because the direction depends on how bonds take the 22:00 SGT data, which can't be known at 20:00.
summary.cant_know: Which way JOLTS lands, and whether bond buyers step in at 5.25% or the selling resumes.
summary.the_call: Flat, and mild: no move bigger than about half a percent. The market ends near where it opens. Chips keep their morning gain but don't add to it. European power chips and Navitas move most; the Singapore banks and big tech move least.
